alarm.screen.description: Press the button below to cycle through the different types of alarms available. When you've found the one you want, click the 'Done' button at the bottom. Supply a redstone pulse (on/off signal) to any side of the box to sound the alarm.
alarm.screen.name: Alarm %s
death.attack.assortedtech.laser.player: %1$s got zapped by a laser whilst trying to escape %2$s
death.attack.assortedtech.spike.player: %1$s walked into a spike whilst trying to escape %2$s
manual.assortedtech.chapter.bridges.acce: An acceleration bridge carries you along faster than walking. Useful for long crossings, and harder to stop on than you expect.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.bridges.deat: A death bridge looks like a trick bridge and hurts anything that touches the beam. It makes a decent doorway for a base, as long as you remember which one you built.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.bridges.grav:
A gravity lift is a beam you step into rather than onto: it pushes whatever is inside it the way it points.

Unlike the others it stops when it meets another gravity lift, so two facing each other make a shaft rather than a fight.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.bridges.lase:
A bridge control shoots a beam when it is given redstone, and the beam is solid ground. It cannot be broken while it is lit, and it stops at the first block in the way.

Right click the control with a block to give the beam that block's texture, and shift right click with an empty hand to put it back. How far it reaches is a config setting.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.bridges.tric: A trick bridge is a laser bridge you fall straight through. It looks solid, which is the entire idea.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.gravity.attr:
Powered, an attractor pulls everything within about twelve blocks towards it. Good for gathering drops, unkind to anything standing nearby.

The directional version only pulls on the face the cone points out of, which is how you aim it down a corridor instead of at yourself.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.gravity.boot: Wearing gravity boots, none of the blocks in this chapter move you at all. Build the machine first and the boots second, or you will spend a while stuck to a ceiling.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.gravity.grav:
A gravitor lifts whatever is near it straight up while it is powered, and lets go the moment it stops. Whatever was in the air then falls the whole way.

The directional version only lifts on the face it points out of.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.gravity.repu:
A repulsor is an attractor run backwards: powered, it pushes everything in range away.

The directional version pushes only out of the face it points, which makes it a wall that mobs cannot walk into.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.redstone.ala:
An alarm sounds while it has power, and goes on any face of a block. Right click it to pick which of the sixteen sounds it makes.

Wired to a sensor it becomes a doorbell, or something considerably less polite.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.redstone.fan:
A fan blows entities away from itself or pulls them towards it. Right click it to set the range and which way it works.

Redstone turns a fan off rather than on, so it runs by default and a lever stops it.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.redstone.fli: A flip flop torch changes state each time it is powered and stays there. One button turns it on, the same button turns it off, which saves building the latch yourself.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.redstone.glo: A glowstone torch lights up when it is powered and goes dark when it is not, the way a redstone lamp does, but you can still walk through it like any torch.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.sensors.sens:
A sensor watches the space in front of it and gives out redstone while something it cares about is there. A light on the face shows when it has seen one.

Which things it cares about is decided by what it is made of, so the recipe is the setting. The next page lists them.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.sensors.trig:
Wood sees everything, including dropped items and arrows. Stone sees anything alive. Iron sees only players.

Mossy cobblestone sees hostile mobs, cobweb sees spiders and their kin, netherrack sees what belongs in the Nether, and end stone sees what belongs in the End.

Gold sees dropped items, emerald sees villagers and wandering traders, prismarine sees what swims, feather sees what flies, and a hay bale sees tamed pets.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.spikes.mater:
What a spike is made of decides how hard it hits. Wood is the weakest at 2 damage and netherite the strongest at 14.

In between, roughly in order: aluminum 3, tin 4, stone 5, gold 6, copper and topaz 6.5, peridot and nickel and lead 7, sapphire 7.5, iron and bronze and ruby 8, invar 8.5, amethyst and silver and electrum 9, diamond and steel 10, emerald and platinum 11.

Every material Assorted Core adds has a spike, so a spare stack of an alloy has somewhere to go.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.spikes.spike:
A spike goes on any face of a block, floor, wall or ceiling, and hurts whatever touches it.

Redstone retracts it. A powered spike sinks flush and does nothing, so a lever turns a corridor from a trap into a hallway and back.
manual.assortedtech.description: Laser bridges, gravity, sensors, spikes and the redstone parts that drive them.
manual.assortedtech.title: Assorted Tech
